final_answer:
A STACK IS A DATA STRUCTURE THAT OPERATES ON A LIFO (LAST IN, FIRST OUT) PRINCIPLE, MEANING THE LAST ITEM ADDED IS THE FIRST ONE TO BE REMOVED. A QUEUE, IN CONTRAST, OPERATES ON A FIFO (FIRST IN, FIRST OUT) PRINCIPLE, WHERE THE FIRST ITEM ADDED IS THE FIRST TO BE REMOVED.

A REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE OF A STACK IS A BROWSER HISTORY STACK. WHEN YOU NAVIGATE BACK, THE BROWSER REMOVES THE CURRENT PAGE (THE LAST ONE YOU VISITED) FIRST. A REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE OF A QUEUE IS A PRINT QUEUE IN AN OFFICE. PRINT JOBS ARE PROCESSED IN THE ORDER THEY ARE RECEIVED, SO THE FIRST JOB SUBMITTED PRINTS FIRST.
